newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish paedophile priest in Dublin for more charges.
newsitem.headline: Irish paedophile priest in Dublin for more charges.

text.p: A paedophile Roman Catholic priest whose crimes helped topple an Irish government returned to Ireland on Friday to face 74 new sexual assault charges after he was freed from prison in British Northern Ireland.

A magistrate in Limavady in County Londonderry approved extradition of Brendan Smyth, 71, after he had served four years in the nearby Magilligan Prison for abusing boys and girls during a 20-year span in the province's capital, Belfast.
Smyth was flown to Dublin for a court appearance on Friday evening after charges of indecent assaults and attempted assaults in the Republic were read out in the Limavady court.
Outside, a crowd jeered Smyth, a member of the Norbertine Canons order.
Revelations of Smyth's assaults on the children of friends shook Irish church authorities and the nation's four million devout Catholics.
The shock intensified when the case brought several other incidents involving sexual abuse by clerics to light.
A furore about a seven-month Irish delay in processing a bid to extradite Smith to Northern Ireland engulfed the government of former prime minister Albert Reynolds in 1994.
It played a key part in bringing down his government in a row over high-level legal appointments.
